about:
Cadrex Chaska, formerly Richlind Metal Fabricators, operates in Chaska, Minnesota. The business was established in 1963 as Richlind Metal Fabricators and was acquired by Cadrex in January 2022, transitioning to the Cadrex brand by August 2022.

The facility provides precision fabrication of finished components and complex assemblies, offering sheet metal fabrication, stamping, CNC machining, welding, plastic injection molding, mechanical assembly, painting and finishing, and system integration and testing. As part of Cadrex, the site draws on a network of 20 facilities totaling 1.5 million square feet and more than 600 machines across the U.S. and Mexico, with capabilities spanning concept development, prototyping, tool design, and custom automation.

The company serves aerospace and defense, medical, data center infrastructure, information communication technology, warehouse automation and robotics, kiosk and gaming, renewable energy and electrical infrastructure, semiconductor equipment, and general commercial industries. Customers include firms such as BAE Systems, referenced in supplier awards.

Richlind was founded on a commitment to engineering support and prototype-to-production processing using shearing, sawing, laser cutting, turning, forming, and machining. Under Cadrex, the operation emphasizes a broad capability set and specialized sector experience to move customer programs from concept to scale quickly.

name: Cal-Maine Farm
old_description: In 1996, Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. became a public company trading on NASDAQ under ticker “CALM”. The Company has demonstrated a long history of impressive profitable growth and operational excellence, reaching a milestone of selling over one billion dozen eggs for the first time in 2014. In addition to organic growth, we have expanded our operations and production capacity through a disciplined acquisition strategy, successfully integrating 26 companies since 1989. We achieved sales of over $2.9 billion with over 1.2 billion dozens sold in fiscal 2026.
about:
Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. is headquartered in Ridgeland, Mississippi. The company traces its roots to 1957 when Fred R. Adams Jr. founded an egg operation in Jackson, Mississippi. In 1996, the company went public on NASDAQ under the ticker CALM and has since pursued a disciplined acquisition strategy, integrating 26 companies since 1989 to expand its production footprint.

The company produces conventional and specialty shell eggs — including cage-free, organic, free-range, pasture-raised, and nutritionally enhanced varieties — as well as prepared egg-based foods, ready-to-eat egg products, and breakfast foods under brands such as Eggland’s Best, Land O’Lakes, Farmhouse Eggs, Crepini, and Van’s Foods. Its operations span 2 breeding facilities, 2 hatcheries, 31 feed mills, 51 shell egg production facilities, 38 pullet growing facilities, 52 processing and packaging facilities, and 5 food manufacturing facilities across multiple states. As of May 2026, the company managed approximately 50 million laying hens, recorded $2.9 billion in annual net sales, and sold 1.2 billion dozen eggs.

Cal-Maine serves retail grocery and foodservice channels nationwide, supplying both consumer-facing brands and ingredient eggs to food manufacturers. Its customer base includes major retailers, foodservice distributors, and commercial food processors.

The company states its purpose is to be the consumer-driven provider of nutritious, affordable, and sustainable eggs and egg-based foods that fit today’s lifestyles, with a vision to ensure healthy, affordable egg choices are accessible to every household every day. It also emphasizes commitments to sustainable operations, hunger relief, and strong corporate governance.

name: California Fine Wire Co.
old_description: , allowing us to support highly regulated medical, aerospace, defense, and industrial markets. Since 1961, CFW has engineered wire solutions that meet exacting performance quality standards.
about:
California Fine Wire Co. was founded in June 1961 by Michael A. Greenelsh in Grover Beach, California. Starting with a single wire drawing machine, the company has grown into a multi‑million‑dollar operation supplying specialty wire and ribbon worldwide.

The company manufactures fine and ultra‑fine wire in round and flat profiles, with diameters from 0.0004″ to 0.125″. Core processes include wire drawing, enamel insulation coating (ceramic, PTFE, nylon, polyester), PTFE insulation, electroplating, flat‑ribbon production, annealing, stranding, cutting, straightening, grinding, polishing, and custom spooling. CFW operates 25 enamel coating machines and maintains an in‑house testing laboratory capable of dimensional measurement to 0.00001″ resolution (±0.00005″ accuracy), tensile testing, and resistance measurement.

CFW serves highly regulated markets including medical devices (implanted cardiac devices, neurological leads), aerospace and defense (lunar missions, satellite components), semiconductor (bonding wire, interconnects), electronics, industrial, marine, and chemical processing. Customers range from research institutions to prime contractors requiring precision wire for critical applications.

Founder Michael A. Greenelsh emphasized that the company’s real specialty is fulfilling customers’ specific needs, no matter how small or unusual. This philosophy, combined with ISO 9001‑certified quality systems and decades‑experienced staff, underpins CFW’s focus on custom solutions for demanding environments.

about:
Caltronics Design & Assembly was founded in 1995 in Stacy, Minnesota, as a family-owned PCB assembly company focused on helping inventors, design engineers, and businesses bring products to market. The firm began by offering complete solutions from concept to prototype and final production, combining design engineering with manufacturing under one roof.

The company provides electronic design, PCB design, and full PCB assembly services, including rapid prototyping, design for test, design for manufacturing, electronic product design, electronics testing, electromechanical assembly, PCB potting, and conformal coating. Production uses a MY700 jet printer, selective solder machine, and 3D automated optical inspection equipment, supporting prototyping through production volumes.

Caltronics serves commercial, defense and aerospace, medical device, military and law enforcement, renewable energy, solar, sports and outdoors, automotive, navigation, and lighting sectors. Customers range from individual inventors to established firms requiring ITAR-compliant assemblies for defense applications.

The company emphasizes big-company experience with small-company service, retaining family ownership while maintaining a global presence. Its ISO 9001:2015 certification and ITAR registration underscore a commitment to quality and compliance, and the firm highlights in-house support from ideation through production as a key differentiator.

name: Capital Electro Circuits Inc
old_description: exceptional craftsmanship, on-time delivery, and customer-focused solutions
about:
Capital Electro Circuits Inc., based in Gaithersburg, Maryland, has been fabricating printed circuit boards since 1985. The company operates as a domestic manufacturer of rigid, flexible, and rigid‑flex PCBs, with a focus on specialty designs that fall outside standard fabrication lines.

The shop produces multilayer boards up to 16 layers, with finished thicknesses up to 1.300 inches, and offers advanced features such as blind/buried vias, edge plating, castellations, and controlled‑impedance structures. It works with a wide range of high‑frequency and high‑reliability laminates — including Rogers, Taconic, Arlon, and TMM series — and provides a full suite of surface finishes (HASL, ENIG, ENEPIG, hard gold, immersion tin/silver). In‑house capabilities cover CAM/DFM, drilling, plating, etching, LPI soldermask, legend printing, CNC routing and scoring, and electrical test (continuity/isolation up to 250 VDC).

The company serves aerospace and defense (including programs for Northrop Grumman, BAE Systems, NASA, Lockheed Martin, Honeywell, Sandia National Laboratories, Booz Allen Hamilton, and the U.S. Army), medical imaging and diagnostics, telecommunications (5G and satellite), automotive and electric‑vehicle systems, and RF/microwave applications up to 100 GHz. It emphasizes 100 % U.S.‑based production for military and avionics work.

Capital Electro Circuits differentiates itself by taking on “specialty” jobs that lack defined manufacturing methods, developing custom processes to deliver working parts on short notice. It maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification, UL recognition, RoHS compliance, ITAR registration, and a conflict‑minerals sourcing policy, and offers blanket orders with split deliveries.

name: Capitol Iron Works
old_description: Based in Rockville, Maryland, Capitol Iron Works specializes in custom ornamental metalwork projects based on unique design ideas, working with ferrous and nonferrous metals, such as stainless steel, aluminum and bronze. The company also works with structural steel and glass. Some of the most common projects include fabrication and installation of architectural railings, stairs, handrails, glass and cable railings, steel fencing, balconies, canopies and automatic gates.
about:
Capitol Iron Works operates from Gaithersburg, Maryland, in the heart of the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. The company was founded in August 2014 by Ronald Vargas, who serves as president and co-owner. Vargas immigrated to the United States from Nicaragua in 2004 and learned welding on the job at Bethesda Iron Works, eventually earning his welding certification before launching his own venture, initially named Capitol Iron Solutions.

The shop specializes in custom ornamental and architectural metalwork, producing railings, stairs, handrails, glass and cable railings, steel fencing, balconies, canopies, and automatic gates. It works with stainless steel, aluminum, bronze, structural steel, wrought iron, and glass, offering powder-coat finishes. The 4,300-square-foot facility houses three fabrication units and a staff of 14. Project values range from $1,000 to $500,000, with revenue projected at $1.5 million for 2018.

Capitol Iron Works serves residential, commercial, and government clients across the D.C., Maryland, and Virginia region. Notable government work includes fabrication and installation of bronze railings for the Rayburn House Office Building under contract with the Architect of the Capitol, the federal agency responsible for the U.S. Capitol Complex. The company also handles restoration of historic metalwork.

Vargas attributes the firm’s rapid growth to customer service, on-time delivery, and a stable, skilled workforce—only one employee has left in four years. He emphasizes a willingness to tackle complex, challenging projects that other shops might avoid, combining fabrication, installation, and restoration under one roof.

name: Capsule Technologies
old_description: Philips Capsule is now part of the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio of solutions – a comprehensive, clinically focused ecosystem designed to enhance care delivery across the healthcare enterprise, with a goal of improving patient outcomes and reducing clinician burnout.
about:
Capsule Technologies, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, operates as part of the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio following its acquisition by Philips. The company focuses on healthcare informatics, providing a vendor-neutral platform that connects medical devices and clinical systems across hospital enterprises.

The company’s portfolio spans medical device integration, clinical surveillance, patient monitoring, virtual care, retrospective analytics, and clinical information systems. Its platform captures live-streaming data from over 1,200 medical devices — including measurements, settings, alarms, and waveforms — and delivers it using industry-standard protocols to more than 100 downstream systems such as electronic health records, clinical information systems, and alarm management tools. Key product lines include Philips Axon, Capsule Neuron, Capsule Vitals Stream, Chart Xpress, the Medical Device Information Platform, eCareManager, Clinical Insights Manager, Capsule Surveillance, and IntelliSpace Critical Care and Anesthesia (ICCA).

Capsule serves hospitals and health systems worldwide, with installations at organizations such as Hamilton Health Sciences in Canada, CoxHealth in the United States, and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in the United Kingdom. Its solutions target acute care environments including intensive care units, perioperative settings, and general wards, aiming to reduce clinician burnout and improve patient outcomes through automated data capture and clinical decision support.

The company emphasizes its vendor-neutral, open ecosystem approach, which allows healthcare providers to leverage existing infrastructure while expanding capabilities incrementally. It also highlights deep clinical and operational experience, stating that its support extends beyond technology to fit workflows and enable clinical staff rather than burden them.

name: Captor Corporation
old_description: has been a trusted name in EMI filters since 1965. Since the beginning, we’ve created innovative EMI filtering products for the world’s most demanding applications, including aerospace and military communications. Today, we offer an extensive product catalog that can easily be customized to your needs without any added cost. Discover our full range of capabilities below.
about:
Captor Corporation was established in 1965 in Tipp City, Ohio, by an engineering-oriented management team that included several experienced veterans. The founders brought deep expertise in electronic filters and military-aerospace communications, and early success allowed the company to build a dedicated manufacturing facility that has since expanded to 35,000 square feet.

The company designs and manufactures custom EMI and EMC filtering solutions, including TEMPEST, HEMP/EMP, and signal-line filters, as well as custom capacitors, inductors, coils, cable assemblies, wire harnesses, electromechanical box builds, and power distribution units. All engineering, production, and testing occur in-house at the Tipp City facility, which houses an advanced all-welded shielded room for pre-compliance testing. Captor has produced over 10,000 custom filter designs and focuses on low-to-medium-volume production.

Captor serves OEMs in aerospace, defense, secure communications, medical equipment, telecommunications, radar systems, and missile-launching programs.

The company emphasizes that custom solutions can be delivered faster and more cost-effectively than many competitors' catalog parts, with no added cost for tailoring. Its mission centers on producing the highest-quality EMI filters, exceeding customer expectations, and maintaining a safe, respectful workplace while continuously improving quality and profitability.

about:
Car Parts New Haven operates as a used and pre-owned auto parts retailer in New Haven, Connecticut. The business serves vehicle owners and mechanics seeking replacement components for damaged or worn parts. While the founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the store has established a presence in the local market and ships parts across the United States and Canada.

The company specializes in used BMW parts and general automotive components, offering both parts sales and whole vehicle sales through its "Car parts And Car Sales" line. Inventory is sourced from salvage and trade-in channels, with the storefront providing a physical location for customer pickup and inspection. No manufacturing or refurbishment processes are performed on-site; the operation functions as a distribution point for pre-owned components.

Primary customers include individual vehicle owners and independent repair shops needing cost-effective replacement parts. The business caters to the automotive aftermarket sector, with a noted focus on BMW models. Shipping coverage extends to all U.S. states and Canada, allowing remote orders beyond the New Haven area.

The store emphasizes customer service and competitive pricing as differentiators, citing word-of-mouth referrals driven by staff knowledge and honesty. Reviews highlight transparent transactions and reliable parts availability, though no formal certifications or quality standards are advertised.
